decisions.reason: §1 pins fs-ext@2.1.1 as a hard dependency of dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, failing at its node-gyp configure build install script because node-gyp finds no Visual Studio — explicitly not plugin code or lockfile corruption.

§2 shows the module-top static import forces fs-ext to resolve and load even on Windows, so skipping scripts leaves the binding missing and crashes at boot; --ignore-scripts is rejected both mechanically and as a blunt global skip.

§3 contrasts the win32 named kernel semaphore (CreateSemaphoreW etc., acquireLockHandleWin32, no flock involved) with POSIX flock(2); Windows fs-ext is dead code at runtime so a stub is lossless, while Windows locking stays on the semaphore and POSIX keeps the native build.

§4 gives the full recipe: pnpm patch on the exact pin, win32-conditional install guard, pure-JS import-safe entry fallback preserving the callable/callback shape, POSIX untouched, registration in pnpm-workspace.yaml (plus build-allow list), and reinstall/module-load/service-boot/semaphore verification.
Explicit non-goals refuse VS and any upstream modification/republish; the pnpm patch is correctly described as repo-local transformation of installed files, not an upstream edit.
§5 cites the full DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 card and maps it 1:1 onto the install-channel fs-ext failure and the Windows patch recipe.

caps.reason: VS installation is an explicit non-goal per the owner's constraint.
--ignore-scripts is explicitly rejected; the patch makes the entry loadable.
Uses the existing repository patch mechanism; upstream stays untouched.
Windows keeps the named semaphore; the no-op fallback only exists where flock is never called and POSIX keeps the native flock.
